title: The Power of Visionary Leadership
paragraphs: I want to talk to you about the power of visionary leadership. Write it down. Visionary leadership power. We want to focus on the key to becoming an effective leader, whether you are a woman or a man. The power of effective visionary leadership. There are two animals on Earth that God has identified with Himself. These are the two most important animals. There is a clear reason why God identified Himself with them: because He is the one who created them. These two animals are both leaders. The first is the eagle.

If you read the constitution of Heaven, which you call the Bible. You will find that throughout that document, God continues to identify himself with the eagle. He never says, " I am a bird of paradise." He never said, " I am a dove." He identified himself only with this huge and powerful bird called the eagle. You will find words like these in the text of the constitution. I will carry you on the wings of eagles.

In another place, God says of himself: “ Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, he will set you upon his wings like an eagle.” In another passage, God says: “ Just as the vulture only gathers around fresh blood, so the Lord will stir you up.” He never gets along with the bathroom. The second animal that God identified himself with is the lion. The lion is also the leader of the animal kingdom. So the eagle is the leader of the bird kingdom and the lion is the leader of the animal kingdom.

Although the lion is not the largest animal in the jungle, nor the most powerful. Not the smartest. It is not the largest animal. However, the lion rules the jungle. The lion is important because the lion destroys all your excuses for not being a leader. You don't need to be the biggest to become a leader. You don't need to be the strongest, the heaviest, the most capable, or even the smartest. However, you can be the leader. So, the lion defies everything they taught you about leadership.

For this reason, God himself identifies with the lion. He says, "I am the Lion of Judah, not the Dog of Judah, not the Giraffe of Judah, not the Elephant of Judah." He identifies with this creature that God created. My question is: Why did God identify so strongly with these two animals? The answer is because He placed certain qualities in these animals that set them apart from others. These qualities are known as leadership traits. This is why it is important to study the lion and to study the eagle.

In fact, these two animals have become my personal friends because they have helped me understand myself, understand God's plan for my life, and understand how I am meant to live. There are two words I want you to associate with these animals. The first for the lion is "attitude." The lion is the king of the animal kingdom because of his attitude. The lion has a deep sense of confidence and courage. He is not afraid of the elephant or the giraffe. He eats the hippopotamus. He takes down the bulls.

He somehow possesses the confidence that he can prey on any animal, no matter how big or how strong. The lion has an attitude of self-confidence. Associate the eagle with the word "vision." Let everyone say: vision. What makes The eagle is dangerous because God has endowed it with the ability to see in great detail from a great distance. The eagle is the only bird on Earth. In fact, it is the only animal on Earth that can see 50 times better than humans.

The eagle can see from five miles away with incredible detail. This is called visual vision. This is why the eagle is the king of birds. It doesn't need to stalk its prey to kill it. It can see its prey from five miles away without the prey even realizing it's being watched. And when the prey realizes it's been watched, it's too late because the eagle swoops down like a bullet. The power of vision is the secret to the eagle's success. So, I want to talk to you about the eagle.

It is the king of birds because of its vision. And if you are to become the leader you were created to be, you don't just need the attitude of a lion, which we will discuss when I return to visit you. But to become the leader you were born to be, you will have to understand the qualities and power of vision. First, let me redefine leadership for you so you have a practical definition of what it means to be a leader, because you were born to be one. Son.

Leadership is defined as the ability to influence others through inspiration born of passion, driven by a vision born of conviction, and resulting from purpose and goal. It's a long sentence, but every word matters. Leadership is the ability to influence people through inspiration, not manipulation. So, true leaders never manipulate people. They inspire them. If anyone tries to control you, they are not a leader. And that includes your spouse. Oh, how embarrassing.

Anyone who feels the need to control you is not a leader. It could be your boss at work. It could be your teacher in class. It could be your pastor. They are not leaders. Anyone who tries to control another human being is not a leader. They are a dictator, a weak, insecure person. True leaders never control people. They inspire people. And how do they inspire people? Through their passion. Where does their passion come from? It comes from a vision they possess. They believe in their vision.

So it creates passion in their lives. Where does the vision come from? The vision comes from a person's deep conviction about why they were born. They believe they were born To do something meaningful. That's what we call conviction. And where does that conviction come from? It comes from discovering a purpose for your life. That you are not a mistake. That you weren't born just to earn a living, pay the bills, and then die. That's why leaders don't think about paying the bills and worrying about money.

Leaders are people who have discovered something more important than a paycheck. Leaders are driven by a sense of purpose and destiny. They believe they were born to solve a problem, to bring healing to humanity, to change a society, to transform a nation, to make an impact in their country. That's leadership. That's why most people today are n't leaders. They just want to earn a living. Leadership. Some of you pastors aren't leaders because you entered the ministry to earn a living. You call it a calling.

And we know it's just making money. You have to ask yourself a question today: Why am I in this ministry? Why is there passion for what I do? Am I willing to die for what I do? Leadership is about conviction. You can be a preacher your whole life and still be useless. Leadership isn't about personal ambition. It's not about personal advancement. Leadership is about a deep conviction about your purpose in life. That I was born to make a difference. Something. I was born to free people from something.

I was born to make a difference in the world, not just to earn a living. Are you a leader? Or do you just have a job? Let me say something interesting. You might want to remember this. Leaders can never retire. Amen. If you can stop what you're doing and still be happy, you're not a leader. Because you can't retire from yourself. And a leader is someone who has discovered themselves. They've discovered who they were born to be. They've discovered what they were born to do. And you can't retire from yourself.

Conviction, passion, vision. I could talk about each of these elements for years without ever going home. Didn't you like that? But I'm going to talk about one of them today. I want to talk about what we call vision. But first, I want you to write this down. I want to give you what I call the leadership process. How to become the leader you were born to be. Everyone, please write this down. First, you have to discover your purpose in life. Without that, you're not a leader.

Second, you have to discover your conviction. That means you have to believe in your purpose. Third, you have to see a vision. The future is born from your purpose and conviction. That vision should give you a passion for life, where you pursue your vision more than your own security. And that vision generates passion. Passion inspires others to believe in you. And when you inspire others, they allow you to influence them. Once you influence people with your passion, that's when they call you a leader.

So, leaders don't seek people. People are drawn to leaders. That's why every great leader in history never sought followers. Why do we love Nelson Mandela? Why are we so excited about the life of Martin Luther King Jr.? Why are we so inspired and moved by Mother Teresa? Why do we admire her so much? Because they inspired us, and therefore influenced us, and we are the ones who called them that. You will never find Nelson Mandela calling himself a leader. He never said so. People call him a leader.

Martin Luther King Jr. would never have called himself a leader. He was just a simple preacher from a small church, but the world calls him a leader. You see, leaders don't call themselves leaders. They are so busy pursuing their vision. So, leadership is a result, not a pursuit. Now, what is the key to this process? Two words. The key to becoming a leader— and I'll give you the secret until I see you again—is purpose and vision.

Until you discover your purpose, which should generate a vision for your future, you are not a leader. Leaders are driven by vision. That's why every politician, every preacher, every father must have a vision if they want to be leaders of their families, businesses, churches, and countries. We are not leaders because we have titles. We are leaders because we have a vision. That's why it's important to ask yourself: Do I have a vision for my life? Here's a phrase I want you to remember.

The greatest gift God gave man is not the gift of sight. It's the gift of vision. I repeat, the greatest gift God gave man is not the gift of sight, it's the gift of vision. What's the difference between sight and vision? An interesting question. Well, first of all, sight is a function of the eyes, but vision is a function of the heart. Sight shows you what is. Vision shows you what could be. Sight is limited to the present. Vision is not limited by the boundaries of the future.

This is why sight must always serve vision. You should never live according to your eyes. Followers live by their eyes. Leaders live by their vision. Sight is limited by what the eye can see. But vision is limited only by the imagination of your heart. This is why leaders are never disturbed by the present. Whatever the circumstances, they are always at peace because they do not live from the reality of the present. No leader should trust their eyes. There is a phrase in our constitution.

For the religious, it is the Bible. Here is what our constitution says: " For we walk by faith, not by sight." The word "walk" means "live." Listen to those words. "For we do not live by sight, but by faith." Now, faith means belief. Leaders do not live by what they see with their eyes. They live by what they believe in their hearts. This is why it is not easy to live with leaders because they do not live where you live. You live in the present. They live in the future.

A leader is always outside the realm of other people's thinking. They are always somewhere else. This is why they are leaders. They do not listen to the noise of the present. They hear the call of the future. True leaders don't trust what their eyes show them. They believe what their vision tells them. The Bible says that the righteous live by faith, not by sight. So when a leader has no money, they never panic. And she never gets depressed. Why? Because she knows it's only temporary. I see a lot.

Leadership requires you to think outside the box. That's why you think living with a leader is easy. It's difficult because the present isn't reality for a leader. For a leader, their vision is more real than the present. I challenge you, young man, to believe in your imagination more than your eyes. Let me pose a few challenges about vision versus sight. Sight confines you to the present, but vision liberates you toward the future. Sight embodies the present. Vision embodies the future.

Sight deals with what is, but vision sees what could be. My question is, what could Papua New Guinea be? Is there anyone in Papua New Guinea who sees another Papua New Guinea? Don't answer the question. Just think about it. When I sat with your Prime Minister yesterday, I asked him three times: What is What is your vision for Papua New Guinea? Because a leader must have a different image. I always judge a leader by their vision, not their programs.

Many of the pastors I 've met don't know what I'm doing when I talk to them, but I analyze them immediately. Sometimes I ask them three questions, and then I can assess who they are right away. Sometimes I ask them the hardest question: What is your vision for your ministry? And most of them answer incorrectly. They say things like winning back the lost at any cost. That's not a vision. And that's why the church is n't growing. I ask the pastors, "What is your vision?" They answer me, "Winning people to Christ."

This is not a vision. This is not a picture of the future. In fact, this is not a vision. This is a mission. And there is a difference between a mission and a vision. In fact, every pastor in this hall has the same mission. That is why it is called the Great Commission, not the Great Vision. Winning the lost is every pastor's mission. This does not make you unique. When I speak to businessmen, I ask them, "What is your vision for your company?" They say things like, "Making a profit." That's not a vision.

Making a profit is every company's mission. No wonder your company went bankrupt. Bill Gates never sought to make money. That wasn't his primary motivation. Steve Jobs, who created the Apple computer, never pursued money. If you had spoken to him before he died and asked, "What is your vision?" His answer would have been to put the power of the internet in the hands of every person on Earth. That's vision. Visionaries deal with the future. How do you measure true vision? How do you know if a vision is real?

I'll give you the answer. Ready? Write this down. Because many people wonder what vision really means. What is a true vision? First, a true vision is a humanitarian cause worth sacrificing oneself for. A true vision is a humanitarian cause worth sacrificing oneself for. In other words, a true vision is when you see a future so important to humanity that you are willing to sacrifice your life to achieve it. That's why true visionaries never live for themselves.

Nelson Mandela had a vision for a South Africa without apartheid. A vision where everyone is equal, without discrimination and without racism. He had a vision for a country where everyone is equal. He saw it and went to prison for it. Sacrifice. Do you see anything, young lady, that's worth going hungry for? Religious people annoy me because they're always thinking about their stomachs. They want to eat all the time. They want a fancy car all the time. They want A beautiful home. They want handouts and gifts.

These are not visionaries. I came to this country and I didn't ask this woman for a single cent. I came here for you. I came because I have a motive to raise the mindset of Third World people so they can believe in themselves. I came because I believe you are great leaders trapped in subservient bodies. If you give me nothing, it won't matter because you are not my source of support. Father of fathers. Leaders are not driven by personal gain.

They are driven by a cause so noble that they are willing to make personal sacrifices for it. Are you a leader, young lady? Think about it. True vision requires sacrifice. Secondly, true vision is a view of the future that is nobler than self-preservation. I want to say this slowly. True vision is a view or image of the future that is nobler than self-preservation. What I mean by that is that true vision is when you see an image of the future that is more important than your survival.

That is why people love Mahatma Gandhi, when he envisioned an India free from British colonial oppression. One man decided that the future The India I see is greater than my own life. So he went to prison. He told them, "I will not eat until my people are free." He began to starve to death in prison. The British tried to force- feed him, but he refused. He shut his mouth and starved for his people. Are you a pastor with a vision? Are you a businessman with a vision?

Are you willing to mortgage your house to make your business succeed? Leadership requires sacrifice. The reason there are so few leaders in this country is that most of us want to preserve ourselves. We don't want to be hated. We want to be liked by everyone. We want to be accepted by everyone. We don't want to cause trouble. We don't want to upset society. We don't want to disrupt tradition. You are useless. You cannot be a leader without breaking with tradition. Leaders are a nuisance.

True leaders are always a problem because they always disrupt the familiar. They break with tradition. They always challenge the prevailing politics. You cannot reach the future by preserving the present. So, leaders are future-oriented. Well, you know, Dr. Munro, our church has been around for 500 years, and I can't change the politics. And traditions, our traditions. Oh, be quiet. No wonder you only have two people in your church. You can't reach the future if you don't leave the present.

Leadership is about movement. You can't lead from where you are. Let me put it another way. You can't lead people to where you are because that's where you are. Leadership means leaving where you are and going somewhere you've never been before. Are you a leader? Third, a true vision isn't selfish ambition. You know, sometimes when you ask people, "What's your vision?" they say, "Oh, to build a big house by the water." That's not a vision. That's ambition.

You ask people, "What's your vision for building a church that can hold 50,000 people?" " That's not a vision. That's ambition. What's your vision? Oh, to become a millionaire before the age of 40. That's not a vision. That's selfish ambition. No wonder no one follows you. A true vision never benefits the visionary. It benefits others. If what you pursue benefits only you, it's not a true vision. Leaders don't live for themselves; they live for the people. They become servants of humanity.

Therefore, a truly great person is always a servant of others. That's why a true vision always serves the people. May leaders emerge from this conference who see Papua New Guinea as greater than their own personal ambitions. Fourth, a true vision isn't for self-promotion. It promotes others. Another example is Nelson Mandela, a good example. His vision for South Africa never promoted himself. He wanted to promote the people of his country.

He wanted to liberate them, give them equality, and provide them with opportunities. He did it for them. That's a true vision. Papua New Guinea, you are at a very critical juncture in your development. Your country is becoming very attractive to the global community, and they are coming for the gold, oil, and gas." And copper. And for your agriculture. The question is: Will you have leaders who care more about you than themselves? Because if they have selfish ambitions, you won't benefit from your resources.

True leaders promote people, not themselves. And fifth, a true vision never destroys people. It builds people up. A true vision will never destroy humanity. That's why I have a problem with people like the late bin Laden. Bin Laden had a vision, but it wasn't a true vision because it destroyed people. The great mind of Muhammad. I've read the Quran. It's a beautiful book. It's a religious book, of course, not a constitution.

And Muhammad writes in his book that anyone who is an infidel should either be killed or enslaved. What kind of vision is that? An infidel means anyone who is n't a Muslim. His vision was that there was no place in the world except for Muslims. Anyone else should be killed or become a slave to a Muslim. What a vision. You can't compare him to Joshua. You know, I was reading the Bible one day and I saw the first terrorists in the Bible. They were worse than bin Laden. There were two of them. They were terrorists.

They are both in the Bible. And both were disciples of Jesus. Can you imagine? Two of his disciples were terrorists. One day they were walking through a village, and two of them came up to him and said, “Teacher, we found some people in the village who worship, but they don’t worship like we do.” Sound familiar? Then they said to Jesus, “Will you call down fire to burn them?” "This is terrorism. They were worse than Mr. Bin Laden. You know, at least Mr.

Bin Laden directed his followers to fly some planes into a building and kill 3,000 people. He ordered his followers to strap bombs to their bodies, go into a market, pull the fuse, and destroy innocent people. At least he did that. That was acceptable. But these men actually asked God to kill them. They were worse. They asked Jesus to bring down fire and burn innocent people. What kind of leadership is that? A true vision never destroys people.

Adolf Hitler had a vision of Europe under one government like the Romans, and he believed he was called by Providence to be the leader of the Third Roman Empire. He killed millions of people to achieve his dream. That's not a true vision. A true vision never destroys people. Would you like to hear Jesus's response to these terrorists? Well, they both called themselves James and John. I think they were from Papua New Guinea. Maybe. They said, 'Let's bring down fire and burn them.' Why?

Because they don't worship like we do." It's no different than what's happening today. There are terrorists in this room. Some of you go around like terrorists. You drive past a mosque. Lord, burn it down. Why are you telling God to burn the building down, man? You're a terrorist. You're no different from them. I've exposed you. That's not leadership. You don't pray for people to be destroyed. And Jesus responded first. He was shocked. Let me quote what he said.

He said, "And Jesus turned to them and said, 'Where did you get this spirit?'" " This is in the Bible. His first answer was a question. Where did you two get this spirit? The word ' spirit' here begins with a lowercase letter. It means behavior or mindset. Where did you get this mindset? He says to kill people. And that's why, with all due respect to Mr. Muhammad, the philosophy of Jesus Christ is superior because he doesn't kill people who disagree with him. Where did you get this spirit?

He said, and then he uttered these words: I didn't come to destroy people's lives, but to save them. Even if they worship differently right now, even if they are still searching, don't kill them while they are searching. Then he made a statement that priests never preach. He said, 'Because I have sheep that are not of this pen.' Why don't you preach this? He was saying to James and John, ' Your position is that of a terrorist.'" I don't kill people. I save people. And they're all mythical.

Some of them are in another pen, still trying to find me. They can't find me if you kill them. So love one another. Love your enemies because they're just temporarily crazy. They're your brothers. They'll come home eventually. A true vision is never destroyed. Ladies and gentlemen, men and women, I want to define for you now what a vision is. We know what it isn't. So what is it? First, a vision is a conceptual view of the future. Now, that word ' conceptual' sounds like a big word. It simply means a picture.

A picture. A vision is a picture of the future. Second, a vision is a visual representation of your purpose. Your purpose is your mission in life. A vision is when you see it in pictures. Third, a vision is a glimpse of why you exist. I have a dream. I see the day coming when Black boys and white girls will walk hand in hand in the streets of Alabama. I have a dream that a person will no longer be judged by the color of their skin but by the substance of their character. I have a dream; Martin Luther King Jr.

saw something. What do you see about Papua New Guinea? Not The one you live in. Is there a leader in your government, in your country, who speaks like this? I have a dream for Papua New Guinea. I see a country with paved streets, happy people, education for all, healthcare available, peace in our fortresses, people happy in their homes, no conflict, no broken homes, no crime. I have a dream. Does anyone have a dream, or do you just want a job? We need leaders, young men. We need leaders, young women.

Pastors, businesspeople. We need leaders, not just entrepreneurs, leaders. This is your country. And you don't like what you see now. People lying on the sides of the streets, young men without jobs, single women pregnant. What is your vision? We need some leaders here. We need people with vision. Where there is no vision, we need leaders. I was sent here to disturb you. What is vision? Vision is realizing your divine mission. Vision is envisioning your preferred future.

Would you rather see what is or what could be? Vision is the ability to see the unseen and to believe With its potential for realization. Vision is about seeing beyond your eyes and living in your imagination. For the benefit of all. Are there leaders in Papua New Guinea? Esther was a beautiful young woman. She was in her twenties and decided to save an entire island and an entire country. Are there young women in their twenties here with a vision for Papua New Guinea like Esther?

Esther knew she might lose her life. I might die. But she was prepared to sacrifice her life for her people. Do you just want to wear clothes, makeup, and dresses, or do you want to change your country? What a woman Esther was. Nehemiah had a job. He was a bartender. But he saw a vision for his country and could no longer stay in his job. A true vision makes your job uncomfortable. He had to leave his job because of his passion for his vision, and he rebuilt his country's walls. Papua New Guinea needs leaders.

Before I conclude, I want to give you the most important principles of leadership and how they relate to vision, which are important principles. The first principle of leadership is purpose. You must discover the secret of your existence and why you were born. I call it your sense of destiny. Second, your passion. Your passion is your personal motivation to pursue your goal. You are willing to sacrifice for it. Third, your principles.

Your principles are the standards and values ​​that you will not violate in pursuit of your vision. And I want to tell you all that principles protect both purpose and passion. Fourth, leadership requires a vision. A vision is a picture of your destiny. It is seeing your future with absolute clarity. Vision is the ultimate goal of leadership. The only reason a leader exists is because of a vision. So where there is no vision, there can be no leader, and where there is a leader, there must be a vision.

If someone claims to be a leader but does not have a clear vision for the future, they are not a leader but a manager. This is why we must embrace a vision. A vision is born. But leadership is born when a vision is embraced. Leadership without a vision is merely managing goals. Leadership is what gives meaning. When a vision comes along, it gives meaning to leadership. It explains leadership. If I ask you why I should follow you, your answer should be vision. It explains leadership. It legitimizes leadership.

This is why, if you want to follow someone, your first question should not be whether they are smart or strong. Rich. The first question is, where are you going? And if they can't answer that question, go somewhere else. You can't follow someone who has no destination. So, leadership gets its meaning and legitimacy from vision. Vision also provides direction and impetus for leadership. The reason there is leadership is vision. So, you must draw up a vision for your life, and your vision must benefit humanity.

When you sit down to write your vision, make sure it benefits others. If it doesn't benefit others, it's not a vision. It's personal ambition. You all came to this earth to improve the lives of humanity. You have to discover what you came here to offer us. There is a talent you possess that we all need. And I say to you women here in Papua New Guinea, your culture has not allowed you to become all that you were born to be. And some men here have a problem with women leading. You are sick.

Esther saved the whole country. Deborah saved her people. Mary gave us Jesus. What is your problem? In fact, let me say to all the pastors clearly, look me in the eyes right now. Look To me. God relies on women for leadership so much that He did n't make the Church a man. The Church is a woman. Ah, let me say it slowly. Jesus Christ is the husband. And the Church is His bride. And He left the world in His bride's hands. Take a deep breath, brothers. That's why I married my wife. I'm an intelligent man.

I married an intelligent, cultured woman with leadership qualities who makes her my wonderful teacher. Ladies and gentlemen, don't stifle other people's vision. Including your spouse. You know, this afternoon I'm going to talk to men, but let me talk to men in front of women for a moment. Many men think women were born to cook for them, to stay in the kitchen. Where in the Bible is that said? Sit up straight. Look at me.

When you read the Constitution, the Bible, you'll find that the cooks in the Bible aren't women. Oh. They're men. You don't believe me, do you? Well, let's prove it. Abraham had a son. His name was "son." What was his name? Isaac. Isaac had two sons. What was his name? Their names? Jacob and Esau. Okay. Isaac is the son of God's promise. And Isaac is about to die. When a man is about to die, he wants the best of everything before he departs. So, Isaac was on his deathbed and said, "Do you know something?"

I am about to die. I know I will die. I want the best meal before I die. "His wife was right there beside him. Man, pull yourself together. Sit up straight now. Talk to me. Isaac said, "I don't want you to cook, woman." You are not good at cooking. I want my son to cook. He cooks the best meal. "And he says, "Well, are men the ones who cook?" "Let's find out. Jesus Christ went to the cross, died, and rose again in his glorified body.

He was sitting on the shore watching the disciples in the boat and said to them, 'Have you caught anything?'" They said: "No." He said, "Throw the net on the other side." "And then they realized that he was the teacher. Peter jumped out of the boat and began running in the water. The book says: "And Jesus was on the shore cooking for them." "Come on, guys. Clap with me. All men who want to be like Jesus, please raise your hands. Okay. That means you should learn to cook. Thank you very much.

Give God a round of applause. He was a cook. Women are leaders and they have a vision. Stop oppressing them. Let them exercise their power. Male and female. Have you ever asked your wife, 'What is your vision?'" "No, she never has because you assume she has no vision, and that's why you're bankrupt. Come on, ladies, clap for me for a few seconds here. Let the energy out. I'm a rich man today because of my wife. Her ideas are amazing. Everyone is born to be a leader. So get over it.

It's a new day in Papua New Guinea. Everyone clap. Come on, men. Clap with me. Shout 'Yes!' Hallelujah. You're meant to be partners in life. Your wife isn't a housemaid. If you're a king, she's automatically a queen, you idiot. All men, clap for the queens in your lives right now. Come on, men, clap loudly. Let's let the queens know we love them. All queens, clap for the great kings around you. Come on, ladies. Leadership begins and ends with vision. Write it down. Leadership what? It begins and ends with vision.

The reason leadership is born is that a person has a vision for the future. And it ends when that vision is achieved. So, leadership is about moving from the present to the future. It's impossible to lead to nothing." Leadership, in fact, presupposes a destination. If you ask me to follow you, you must be going somewhere. In reality, leadership without a destination is not leadership; it is mere movement. Leadership without a destination is meaningless activity. Leadership without a destination is simply movement.

I heard a saying, and I agree with it: if you don't know where you're going, any road will take you there. If you have no aim, you'll never miss it. Leaders know where they are going. They have a destiny and a purpose. They have a picture of the future. They know what they want to achieve and they know exactly what they want to do. They have a conceived and deliberate vision. They see the future. Whoever leads without a vision is simply wandering aimlessly. Leadership without a vision is meaningless activity.

Leadership without a vision is a misuse of talent and human resources. Some of you pastors, I warn you, be careful. You can greatly misuse your people because if you collect their donations and don't take them anywhere, you are thieves. Leadership is about the destination, not the programs. Give us leaders, Lord. If your government collects taxes but doesn't take the country to The future is not about the future; it's a waste of people's resources.

If you're collecting donations at your church and you don't have a vision for the future, that's a waste of people's resources. If you have musicians playing for you every week and people at the door acting as guides, but you're not taking the church into the future, you're wasting those people's talents. Leadership is n't about maintaining the status quo; it's about movement. Leadership is exemplified in this statement by Jesus Christ. He said, "If a blind man leads a blind man, both will fall into a pit."
